messages:
noah-t: heads-up: spotted a gap in our SDLC flow. suppressed SAST findings are not being surfaced when a related deploy hits prod errors.

maria-l: hm. we discussed auto-reopen weeks ago but never landed the rules. what conditions would trigger reopen?

ana-r: two triggers i'd expect: 1) related prod error spike (5xx or latency p95 up) correlated to the file/service; 2) exploitability increase (from triage or external CVE feed).

tj-s: + add: if DAST shows runtime repro possibility (auth bypass or unsafe redirect) then immediate reopen regardless of suppression age.

sec-bot: scan alert: nightly-sast-721 produced 12 findings (2 suppressed, id=F-7a3, F-2b1). https://ci/reports/721

ops-bot: note: current artifact fetch IAM role (scanner_reader_v1) grants repo-wide read. request to minimize scope pending.

maria-l: proposal: create a narrow service role scanner_artifact_reader that can read artifacts only when request includes evidence_claim header and signed request token. add condition: resource.name.startsWith('projects/redwood/repos/') && resource.labels.scan=true

noah-t: we must map that to KMS usage too. ephemeral unwrap keys only if KMS request origin==scanner-service and subject includes scan_id. audit entry should contain scan_id and requestor.

ana-r: (typo correction) ana-r: agree with KMS wrap policy. we should also require HSM-backed wrapping keys for production artifacts.

sec-bot: policy stub created: https://infra/docs/scan-rbac-policy.md (draft)

maria-l: retention question: compliance wants 2y for security-critical evidence, legal wants indefinite hold on request, infra estimates 2y full-artifact cost ~$1.6k/mo. ops: can we tier artifacts?

ops-bot: yes. tiering available: metadata+snippet (180d), compressed trace (365d), full artifact (30d) by default. legal_hold tag overrides.

noah-t: sounds reasonable. we should ensure every suppression stores a minimal audit bundle: finding_id, repo, commit, suppressor, suppression_reason, suppress_expires_at. searchable.

maria-l: agreed. also add provenance header: original_pipeline, scanner_version, ruleset_hash. retention for provenance = 3y.

sec-bot: sample webhook payload for triage consumer:
```
{
  "finding_id": "F-7a3",
  "service": "payments-svc",
  "severity": "high",
  "status": "suppressed",
  "repo": "github.com/redwood/payments",
  "commit": "b6f9a8c",
  "file": "payment/processor.go:248",
  "snippet": "json.Unmarshal(userInput, &obj)",
  "artifact_link": "gs://scans/artifacts/F-7a3.enc",
  "artifact_wrap": "kms://wrapkeys/scan-prod-2026",
  "provenance": "nightly-sast-721",
  "suppressor": "ana-r",
  "suppress_reason": "false positive - fuzzed inputs",
  "suppress_expires_at": "2026-08-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

ana-r: on auto-reopen logic outline: if suppressed && (exploitability_score >= 7 || prod_error_correlation >= 0.8) then reopen ticket in SECURITY-INCIDENTS and notify oncall. also bump retention and mark legal_hold=false? (no, legal_hold shouldn't change automatically).

tj-s: implement correlation by joining telemetry service traces to the repo path via service mapping. can instrument tracing to emit file hint when errors originate in instrumented code paths.

maria-l: for rollout: 1) land RBAC narrow role + IAM audit annotations; 2) wire webhook consumer to create SECURITY-INCIDENTS tickets; 3) enable auto-reopen in canary org for 2 services; 4) monitor false reopen rate for 2 weeks.

noah-t: timeline? next sprint for RBAC + webhook stubs, canary in sprint+1.

ops-bot: created issue INFRA-836 with IAM template and KMS wrap policy. reviewers: @maria-l @tj-s @ana-r.

maria-l: i'll draft the short RFC (retention + auto-reopen + tiering) and share in #eng-security for signoff. aim to include example queries for auditors.

sec-bot: FYI: CVE feed integration task queued (SEC-431) to surface external exploitability scores into our triage.

ana-r: thanks all. leaving a checklist entry: add e2e unit for suppress-and-reopen scenario to our test harness. :white_check_mark:

noah-t: perfect. closing thread, will follow up on RFC. :rocket:
